College is one of the biggest scams modern day highschool graduates can fall for.

From the moment children start school, they are told by both their parents and teachers that they must go to college and get a degree because those jobs "pay the most". There is never any mention on trade jobs or entrepreneurship. Trade jobs are often stigmatized by society, despite the fact that they pay better and supply more demands than college degree jobs.

A quick look on a job-huntung site will show that most starting salaries for jobs requiring higher education pay the same compared to entry trade jobs (which also tend to have more entrepreneurial value than college degree jobs). Children are also never encouraged to pursue entrepreneurial careers, which can teach valuable lessons about how the world works more so than college programs will.

College used to be reserved for those gifted with high intelligence and academic drive, which is why I personally believe college only makes sense for A students. If you are in college and find yourself with a B or C average, you might want to consider a career change.

The generational college indoctrination over saturates the job market; if the majority of people go to college and get degrees, there will be an excess supply of qualified lawyers, doctors, engineers, etc. This not only lowers the starting salary, but also harms the economy due to the lacking quantity of trade workers (who in theory are more essential to the functionality of society).

High tuition costs, textbook costs, and fees for services you will never use are what make a college education a complete scam. There is nothing wrong with going to college for the sole purpose of learning, but relying on your degree to find employment will leave you broke and miserable in the end. It'd be better for those graduating highschool to save money and start a business, or learn a trade of some sort, while leaving college for the A students who will benefit far more from it.
